ilerComplianceLevel)` method, but in doing so it dropped the `JavaVersion.toVersion(...)` conversion and called `.toString()` directly on the raw `String` parameter — which is a no-op (`

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 7434506f7fd3a069f899c1d535eaf0a876306c6f

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `ConventionJdt.java` with `git log --oneline -- <file>`, which showed the relevant commits. The fix (333cd0d) changes `compilerComplianceLevel.toString()` to `JavaVersion.toVersion(compilerComplianceLevel).toString()`, so I looked for where the code last used `JavaVersion.toVersion(...)` correctly and where that conversion was lost.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `e4cd898` originally introduced `compilerComplianceLevel(String)`, which correctly converted the input to a `JavaVersion` object (`this.compilerComplianceLevel = JavaVersion.toVersion(compilerComplianceLevel);`) and later called `.toString()` on that `JavaVersion` instance inside `JavaComplianceAction`.

Commit `7434506` ("Moved new JdtConvention actions to be local, where possible") refactored this to inline the logic directly inside the `compilerComplianceLevel(String compilerComplianceLevel)` method, but in doing so it dropped the `JavaVersion.toVersion(...)` conversion and called `.toString()` directly on the raw `String` parameter — which is a no-op (`someString.toString() == someString`). This silently discarded the version normalization (e.g., converting `"1.6"` into the canonical form `JavaVersion` produces), causing the Eclipse JDT compliance properties to receive whatever raw string the user passed in, unnormalized.

**(3) Evidence:** The fix commit 333cd0d only touches the line `JDT_COMPLIANCE_PROPS.forEach(p -> props.put(p, compilerComplianceLevel.toString()));`, restoring it to `JavaVersion.toVersion(compilerComplianceLevel).toString()`, and removes now-unused `LinkedHashMap`/`Map` imports that were vestiges of the pre-7434506 design. This exactly reverses the regression introduced in 7434506, where the `JavaVersion` conversion was dropped when the code was inlined from the field-based `JavaComplianceAction` class into the local lambda.
